title: The peace to both sides
hookLine: turn right, then left: peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah
last: TASHAHHUD — PEACE ON US AND THE GOOD.

lines: HOW DO YOU WALK BACK OUT?
cards: How do you end a phone call with someone you love? Not just click. You say bye, and bye, and okay, bye, love you, bye.
Endings matter. They tell the other person how you're leaving. The prayer's door closed behind you at the start, with Allahu akbar.
For a few minutes you've been somewhere else: standing, bowing, on the floor, sitting. Now you have to come back into the room. How does the prayer let you walk back out?

teach.h: TASLIM — FROM THE ROOT OF SALAAM.
teach.b: The ending is called taslim, from the same root as salaam, the very first word on this path.
In the most common form, at the end of the last sitting, the person turns the head to the right and says: as-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah.
Then to the left, and again.

Remember the hadith from day one hundred one: the prayer's opening is the takbir, and its closing is the taslim. The door that closed with Allahu akbar opens again with peace. Who is the greeting for?
Scholars give a few answers: the angels, whom the tradition places on the right and left of every person; the people praying beside you in the line; Muslims everywhere.
The words are plural, you all, so there's room for all of them. A small story in Sahih Muslim shows how ordinary it's meant to be.
A companion named Jabir said that when they prayed with the Prophet ﷺ, they used to wave their hands at the salam, to one side and the other.
The Prophet asked why they were waving like restless horses flicking their tails, and said it was enough to rest the hand on the thigh and greet your brother on your right and on your left.
So the prayer doesn't end with a request, or a flourish.

teach.h: PEACE TO THE PERSON BESIDE YOU.
teach.b: It ends with you looking at the people beside you and wishing them peace and mercy.

how: Muslims end every prayer by turning the head to the right and then to the left, saying as-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah each time, greeting the angels and the worshippers on either side.

o: the closing greeting of peace, right then left
a bow of the head to the imam at the end
the blessing the imam says over the room

games.q: what's inside the taslim — tap the pairs.
p: the closing, from the root of salaam

s: the prayer ends by turning the head right, then left
with as-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah each time.
the companions were told to wave their hands at the salam
they used to, and the Prophet ﷺ told them resting the hand on the thigh was enough (Muslim).
the greeting is meant only for the angels
scholars say it includes the angels, the people beside you, and Muslims everywhere.

games.q: you're praying with the companions, and at the salam everyone waves their hands to each side. the Prophet ﷺ notices. what does he say?
o: rest your hand on your thigh and greet the person beside you
games.why: he asked why they waved like restless horses' tails, and said it was enough to greet your brother on the right and left (Muslim).

practice: Sit with your hands on your thighs and turn your head slowly to the right; if you pray, say as-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah, and if not, wish well whoever is on that side of you, in the next room, the next house, the next city.
Then turn slowly to the left and do the same, and come back to center.

wordCard.voice: Taslim. The closing of the prayer: peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah, turning right, then left. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah, said to the right and to the left.

carryVoice: Your line: peace, both ways. Even the way out of the prayer is a greeting. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 431 (Jabir: waving at the salam; greet the one on your right and left)
Sunan Abi Dawud 61; Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3 (its closing is the taslim)
Qur'an 50:17 (the two receivers on the right and the left)
